events.title: Early Stone Age Inhabitants
events.description: Early humans in the Mali region used stone tools, living by hunting and gathering. Archaeological evidence shows this area had rich natural resources and early human activities. These societies were small-scale, highly mobile, adapted to local environment.

events.title: Neolithic Period and Early Agriculture
events.description: The region began showing agricultural activities, people started cultivating crops and domesticating animals. Pottery-making technology emerged, settlements became more permanent. Social organization became more complex, social stratification began appearing.

events.title: Formation of Trans-Saharan Trade Routes
events.description: As climate change affected the Sahara region, early trade routes began to form. Nomadic peoples moved between oases, establishing early commercial networks connecting North Africa with sub-Saharan Africa. These routes laid the foundation for later gold and salt trade.

events.title: Early Iron Age Settlement
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human settlement in present-day Mali during the Iron Age. The fertile Niger River valley attracted early agricultural communities who developed iron-working technology and farming practices. These early settlers laid the foundation for the great empires that would later emerge.

events.title: Rise of Ancient Djenné
events.description: Djenné in the inland Niger Delta became an important trading and craft center. Archaeological excavations reveal the city had advanced urban planning, pottery manufacturing, and metalworking technologies. Djenné is one of West Africa's oldest continuously inhabited cities.

events.title: Period of Political Fragmentation
events.description: After the Songhai Empire's collapse, the Mali region fragmented into numerous small kingdoms and chieftaincies. The Bamana Kingdom, Masina Fulani state, Segu Kingdom, and others emerged successively. This period was characterized by political fragmentation, frequent warfare, and the flourishing of the slave trade.

events.title: Ghana Empire Influence
events.description: Although the Ghana Empire's core was located in present-day Mauritania and Senegal, its influence extended into western Mali. Ghana controlled trans-Saharan trade routes, particularly gold and salt trade, bringing prosperity and cultural exchange to the region.

events.title: Soninke Merchant Network Expansion
events.description: Soninke merchants established extensive trade networks connecting sub-Saharan gold mines with North African markets. They developed sophisticated commercial practices including credit systems and caravan organization. Soninke merchants played a key role in spreading Islam and Arab culture.

events.title: Introduction of Islam
events.description: Islam began entering the Mali region through trans-Saharan trade routes. Muslim merchants and scholars brought new religion, writing systems, and commercial practices. Islam gradually merged with local traditional beliefs, creating a unique religious culture.

events.title: Development of Gao Kingdom
events.description: Gao, located in the eastern Niger River region, became an important trading center and political entity. The Gao Kingdom controlled eastern trade routes and established close ties with Arab merchants from North Africa. The city later became the capital of the Songhai Empire.

events.title: Rise of the Mandinka People
events.description: The Mandinka people (Mande) began establishing political organizations in the upper Niger River region. They developed complex social structures including age-grade systems, secret societies, and oral history traditions. The Mandinka became the core ethnic group of the later Mali Empire.

events.title: Kouroukan Fouga Charter
events.description: At the Kouroukan Fouga assembly, Mandinka clan leaders gathered to create a legal document known as the 'Mande Charter.' This charter established social order, rights and obligations, and governance principles, considered one of the world's earliest constitutions, laying the legal foundation for the Mali Empire.

events.title: Sundiata Keita Establishes Mali Empire
events.description: The legendary hero Sundiata Keita established the Mali Empire after defeating Sumanguru of the Sosso Kingdom. According to the oral epic 'Sundiata Epic,' he united the Mandinka clans and established a powerful centralized state. The Mali Empire became one of West Africa's most powerful political entities.

events.title: Sundiata's Reign
events.description: During Sundiata Keita's reign, the Mali Empire rapidly expanded, controlling important trade routes and gold mines. He established an effective administrative system, promoted agricultural development and craft prosperity. Sundiata's rule laid the foundation for Mali Empire's golden age.

events.title: Rise of Timbuktu
events.description: Timbuktu began emerging as a trading center, its strategic location on the Niger River making it an important hub connecting North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa. The city attracted merchants, scholars, and craftsmen from various regions, gradually developing into an important commercial and cultural center.

events.title: Mansa Musa's Reign
events.description: Mansa Musa's (Musa I) reign was the golden age of the Mali Empire. He was a devout Muslim who greatly promoted Islamic education and culture. Under his rule, the Mali Empire reached its greatest extent, stretching from the Atlantic coast to the Niger bend, controlling rich gold and salt mines.

events.title: Mansa Musa's Pilgrimage
events.description: Mansa Musa undertook his famous pilgrimage to Mecca, displaying the Mali Empire's enormous wealth. During his stop in Cairo, he distributed so much gold that local gold prices fell for ten years. This pilgrimage made the Mali Empire famous in the Islamic world and on European maps, establishing its reputation as a wealthy kingdom.

events.title: Timbuktu Academic Center
events.description: With Mansa Musa's support, Timbuktu developed into an important Islamic academic center. Sankore University attracted scholars from throughout the Islamic world, and libraries housed hundreds of thousands of manuscripts. Timbuktu became the 'City of Scholars,' making important contributions in astronomy, mathematics, jurisprudence, and literature.

events.title: Decline of Mali Empire
events.description: In the 15th century, the Mali Empire began declining. Internal succession disputes, provincial governors' independence tendencies, and the rise of the Songhai Empire all weakened central authority. Changes in trade routes and Portuguese activities on the West African coast also affected the empire's economic foundation.

events.title: Songhai Empire Rule
events.description: The Songhai Empire gradually replaced Mali as West Africa's dominant power. Songhai controlled important cities like Timbuktu, Gao, and Djenné, continuing trans-Saharan trade traditions. The Songhai Empire reached its peak under Askia Muhammad until being defeated by Moroccan forces in 1591.

events.title: Moroccan Invasion
events.description: The Moroccan Saadi dynasty sent an army equipped with firearms across the Sahara, defeating the Songhai Empire at the Battle of Tondibi. This invasion ended the era of great West African empires, leading to political fragmentation and reorganization of trade routes. The Moroccans established a pasha system to rule the Timbuktu region.

events.title: Establishment of Bamana Kingdom
events.description: The Bamana people established a kingdom at Segu, becoming an important force in the middle Niger River region. The Bamana Kingdom was known for its strong military organization and agricultural production, controlling important trade routes. The kingdom maintained traditional African religions, resisting Islamization.

events.title: Seku Amadu's Jihad
events.description: Fulani religious leader Seku Amadu launched a jihad in the Masina region, establishing the Masina Empire. This was part of the West African Fulani jihad movement aimed at establishing pure Islamic states. The Masina Empire controlled the fertile inland Niger Delta region.

events.title: El Hadj Umar's Conquests
events.description: Toucouleur religious leader El Hadj Umar Tall launched a jihad, conquering the Segu Bamana Kingdom and Masina Empire, establishing the Toucouleur Empire. His conquests unified most of present-day Mali but also brought intense religious and political conflicts.

events.title: Samori Ture's Resistance
events.description: Mandinka warrior Samori Ture established the Wassoulou Empire, becoming an important force resisting French colonial expansion. He employed guerrilla tactics and modern weapons, fighting French forces for nearly twenty years. Samori was called the 'Napoleon of West Africa.'

events.title: French Colonial Conquest
events.description: France began systematic conquest of the Mali region, a process lasting fifteen years. French forces defeated various indigenous kingdoms and empires, including the Toucouleur Empire and Samori's Wassoulou Empire. Samori's capture in 1898 marked the end of organized resistance.

events.title: Establishment of French Sudan
events.description: France formally established the French Sudan colony, including most of present-day Mali. The colonial government implemented direct rule, introducing French administrative systems, education, and economic policies. Traditional political structures were weakened or completely destroyed.

events.title: Incorporation into French West Africa
events.description: French Sudan became part of the French West Africa federation, with the governor-general based in Dakar. This administrative reorganization strengthened French control over West Africa, promoted economic integration between colonies, but also deepened dependence on France.

events.title: Colonial Administrative Reform
events.description: France introduced a new administrative system in French Sudan, establishing administrative districts (cercles) and subdivisions. Traditional chiefs were integrated into the colonial system as auxiliary administrators, which weakened traditional power structures but also created a new political elite class.

events.title: World War I Conscription
events.description: France conscripted tens of thousands of soldiers from French Sudan to fight in World War I. Many Malian soldiers fought on European battlefields, an experience that broadened their horizons but also caused human losses and social upheaval. War service later became a basis for demanding political rights.

events.title: Anti-Conscription Rebellion
events.description: Large-scale rebellions erupted across West Africa against forced conscription and high taxes. In French Sudan, populations in some regions refused military service and launched armed resistance. French colonial authorities violently suppressed these rebellions and strengthened military control.

events.title: Expansion of French Education
events.description: The colonial government began establishing more French-language schools in urban centers to train local elites to serve colonial administration. These schools created a French-educated African intellectual class who later became leaders of nationalist movements.

events.title: Forced Labor System
events.description: The French colonial government implemented a forced labor system, requiring Africans to work without pay for public works and private enterprises. This system caused enormous human and social costs, generating widespread discontent and resistance. Many people fled their homes to avoid forced labor.

events.title: Head Tax System
events.description: The colonial government implemented universal head taxes, forcing Africans into the cash economy. To pay taxes, many people were forced into seasonal migrant labor or cash crop cultivation. This system profoundly changed traditional economic and social structures.

events.title: Establishment of Office du Niger
events.description: France established the Office du Niger, launching a massive irrigation project aimed at transforming Mali into a cotton and rice production base. This project required extensive forced labor and changed the agricultural landscape of the inland delta region.

events.title: Cash Crop Promotion
events.description: The colonial government vigorously promoted cotton cultivation, transforming Mali into a raw material supplier for French textile industry. This policy changed traditional agricultural structures and increased farmers' economic burden, but also brought some modernization.

events.title: Bamako-Dakar Railway Completion
events.description: The railway connecting Bamako to Dakar was completed, one of the most important infrastructure projects of the colonial period. The railway facilitated goods transport and population movement, but also deepened the exploitative nature of colonial economy, integrating Mali more tightly into the French economic system.

events.title: Vichy France Rule
events.description: During World War II, French West Africa was under Vichy France rule. Economic difficulties intensified during this period, with increased forced labor and requisitions. The war also exposed the limitations of French power, planting seeds for later independence movements.

events.title: Brazzaville Conference Impact
events.description: Free France convened a conference in Brazzaville to discuss colonial reforms. Though the conference rejected the possibility of independence, it promised political and economic reforms. This meeting sparked demands for political rights among French Sudan intellectuals and veterans.

events.title: World War II Veterans Return
events.description: Thousands of Malian soldiers returned from European and Asian battlefields. Their war experiences and expectations for equal treatment became catalysts for postwar political awakening. Veterans' organizations became important forces in early nationalist movements.

events.title: Abolition of Forced Labor
events.description: France passed the Houphouët-Boigny Law, formally abolishing forced labor in the colonies. This reform was an important response to African demands for rights, marking a major shift in colonial policy and improving conditions for millions of people.

events.title: French Union Status
events.description: After the war, French Sudan gained overseas territory status within the French Union. The new constitution granted limited autonomy and established local assemblies. Though limited, this reform provided space for political participation and nationalist movement development.

events.title: Formation of Sudanese Union
events.description: Modibo Keita and others formed the Sudanese Union political party, becoming Mali's most important political organization. The party advocated African unity, socialism, and anti-colonialism, playing a key role in the independence movement.

events.title: RDA Branch Established in Mali
events.description: The pan-African party African Democratic Rally (RDA) established a branch in French Sudan. The organization advocated African unity and anti-colonialism, becoming an important platform for mobilizing popular political participation. RDA activities laid the organizational foundation for independence movements.

events.title: Loi-Cadre Reforms
events.description: France passed the Loi-Cadre, granting greater autonomy to African colonies. French Sudan established a semi-autonomous government with Modibo Keita as head of government. This reform accelerated the decolonization process.

events.title: French Community
events.description: In de Gaulle's constitutional referendum, French Sudan chose to join the French Community, gaining internal autonomy status. This was an important step toward complete independence while maintaining special relations with France.

events.title: Formation of Mali Federation
events.description: French Sudan merged with Senegal to form the Mali Federation, named after the ancient Mali Empire. This federation aimed to create a larger political entity, but the two countries had differences in political ideology and economic policy.

events.title: Mali Federation Independence
events.description: The Mali Federation gained independence from France, with Modibo Keita as president. Independence celebrations were held in Dakar, marking the end of French colonial rule in West Africa. However, tensions within the federation soon became apparent.

events.title: Mali Federation Dissolution
events.description: Due to political differences, the Mali Federation dissolved just two months after independence. Senegal withdrew from the federation, and the French Sudan portion continued using the name Mali, with Modibo Keita becoming president of the Republic of Mali.

events.title: Modibo Keita's Socialist Experiment
events.description: Keita's government implemented radical socialist policies including nationalization, collective agriculture, and planned economy. The government had tense relations with France, withdrew from the franc zone, and issued its own currency. These policies led to economic difficulties and social discontent.

events.title: Moussa Traoré Military Coup
events.description: Young officer Moussa Traoré led a military coup, overthrowing Modibo Keita's government. The coup received popular support because Keita's socialist policies had led to economic crisis. Traoré established a military government, promising to restore economic stability.

events.title: Rejoining the Franc Zone
events.description: Traoré's government abandoned the previous government's radical policies, rejoined the franc zone, and restored close relations with France. This decision stabilized the currency and improved economic conditions but also increased dependence on France.

events.title: Sahel Drought Disaster
events.description: Severe drought struck the Sahel region, including northern Mali. The drought caused massive famine, livestock deaths, and population migration. This disaster exposed Mali's economic vulnerability and sensitivity to climate change.

events.title: Formation of Democratic Union of Mali
events.description: Traoré established a one-party state, forming the Democratic Union of Mali as the only legal party. This system concentrated political power but also limited political participation and freedom of expression.

events.title: Economic Structural Adjustment
events.description: Under pressure from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, Mali implemented economic structural adjustment programs. Reforms included privatization, trade liberalization, and reduced public spending. These measures improved macroeconomic indicators but also exacerbated social inequality.

events.title: Border War with Burkina Faso
events.description: Mali and Burkina Faso fought a brief war over the Agacher Strip border dispute. This conflict, called the 'Christmas War,' lasted five days and caused hundreds of deaths. The International Court of Justice later ruled on the border demarcation.

events.title: Beginning of Tuareg Rebellion
events.description: Northern Tuareg people began armed rebellion, demanding greater autonomy and development aid. The rebellion's roots included political marginalization, economic underdevelopment, and cultural oppression. This conflict would continue to trouble Mali for decades.

events.title: Democratic Revolution
events.description: Mass demonstrations and military coup overthrew Traoré's government, ending 23 years of military rule. The transitional government promised democratization and multi-party elections. This event was called Mali's 'Democratic Revolution.'

events.title: Alpha Oumar Konaré Elected President
events.description: In Mali's first multi-party democratic election, Alpha Oumar Konaré was elected president. The new constitution established a multi-party democratic system, guaranteeing basic rights and freedoms. Konaré's government was committed to democratic consolidation and economic reform.

events.title: Peace Agreement with Tuareg
events.description: The government signed a peace agreement with Tuareg rebels, ending six years of armed conflict. The agreement included weapons destruction ceremonies, rebel integration, and northern development plans. However, implementation of the agreement was not entirely successful.

events.title: Amadou Toumani Touré Elected President
events.description: Former general Amadou Toumani Touré won the presidential election, becoming Mali's third democratically elected president. Touré promised to continue the democratization process, fight corruption, and promote economic development.

events.title: New Tuareg Rebellion
events.description: Northern regions again erupted in Tuareg rebellion, led by Ibrahim Ag Bahanga's Democratic Alliance for Change in Mali. Rebels complained that the 1996 peace agreement had not been adequately implemented, demanding greater autonomy and resource allocation.

events.title: Algerian-Mediated Peace Agreement
events.description: Under Algerian mediation, the government signed a new peace agreement with Tuareg rebels. The agreement promised increased northern investment, rebel integration into national forces, and greater local autonomy.

events.title: Military Coup
events.description: Officers led by Captain Amadou Sanogo overthrew President Touré, citing government incompetence in the northern conflict. The coup received some popular support but was strongly condemned and sanctioned by the international community.

events.title: MNLA Rebellion
events.description: The National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad (MNLA) launched a new rebellion, demanding northern independence. Rebels were supported by heavy weapons and fighters returning from Libya. Government forces performed poorly in the north, losing large territories.

events.title: Azawad Independence Declaration
events.description: The MNLA declared independence for the northern three regions (Kidal, Gao, Timbuktu), establishing the state of Azawad. However, this declaration was not recognized by any country, and the MNLA soon lost control of the region.

events.title: Islamist Groups Control North
events.description: Islamist extremist groups including Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb, Ansar Dine, and Movement for Unity and Jihad defeated the MNLA and controlled northern Mali. These groups implemented strict Islamic law, destroyed cultural heritage, and drew international attention.

events.title: French Military Intervention (Operation Serval)
events.description: At the request of Mali's transitional government, France launched Operation Serval to prevent Islamist extremist groups from advancing south. French forces quickly recaptured major cities, but guerrilla warfare and terrorist attacks continued. This intervention received international support.

events.title: UN Peacekeeping Force Deployment
events.description: The UN Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali (MINUSMA) began deployment, replacing the African-led International Support Mission to Mali. The peacekeeping force's mission included protecting civilians, supporting political processes, and assisting humanitarian aid.

events.title: Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta Elected President
events.description: In internationally supervised presidential elections, Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta won, becoming the first democratically elected president after the crisis. The election was considered free and fair, marking the restoration of democratic processes.

events.title: Algiers Peace Agreement
events.description: The government signed the 'Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation in Mali' with northern armed groups, aimed at ending the northern conflict. The agreement included power-sharing, development plans, and security arrangements, but implementation proved difficult.

events.title: Operation Serval Becomes Operation Barkhane
events.description: France expanded Operation Serval into Operation Barkhane, covering the entire Sahel region. This operation aimed to combat transnational terrorism threats, but Mali's security situation remained unstable.

events.title: President Keïta Re-elected
events.description: Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta won re-election in the presidential election, but the electoral process was affected by security issues and opposition protests. Keïta promised to continue the peace process and economic development.

events.title: Military Coup Overthrows Keïta
events.description: Military officers staged a coup, arresting President Keïta and the Prime Minister, forcing them to resign. The coup's background included ongoing security crisis, economic difficulties, and political discontent. The international community again imposed sanctions on Mali.

events.title: Bah N'daw Becomes Transitional President
events.description: Under international pressure, the military government appointed retired colonel Bah N'daw as transitional president, promising elections within 18 months. However, the military still held actual power.

events.title: Second Military Coup
events.description: The military staged another coup, arresting transitional president Bah N'daw and the Prime Minister, accusing them of failing to fulfill reform promises. Colonel Assimi Goïta became the new transitional president, extending the transition period.

events.title: France Announces End of Operation Serval
events.description: French President Macron announced the end of Operation Serval and reorganization of military presence in the Sahel region. This decision reflected France's dissatisfaction with Mali's political situation and questioning of military intervention effectiveness.

events.title: Cooperation with Russian Wagner Group
events.description: Mali's military government established cooperation with the Russian Wagner mercenary group, causing concern among Western countries. This shift marked a major adjustment in Mali's foreign policy, from traditional French influence toward Russia.

events.title: Complete French Military Withdrawal
events.description: The last French troops withdrew from Mali, ending nearly a decade of military presence. The French withdrawal marked a new phase in Mali's security situation but also raised concerns about a security vacuum.

events.title: UN Peacekeeping Force Withdrawal
events.description: At Mali's government request, the UN Security Council decided to end the MINUSMA mission, and peacekeeping forces began withdrawal. This decision ended ten years of UN peacekeeping presence, but security challenges remained severe.

events.title: Ongoing Security Challenges
events.description: Despite military government claims of progress, Mali still faces severe security challenges. Terrorist organizations continue operating in northern and central regions, with ongoing civilian casualties. Economic difficulties, humanitarian crisis, and political instability are intertwined, and Mali's future remains uncertain. The international community calls for restoration of democratic rule, but the military government has extended the transition period to 2026.
